lines.text: Her beloved knocks at night, his head drenched with dew, and puts his hand to the latch.
She rises and opens the door, her fingers dripping with myrrh, but her beloved has turned and gone.
The watchmen find her, beat her and take her veil, and she asks the daughters of Jerusalem to tell him she is sick with love.
Asked how her beloved is better, she says his head is purest gold, his eyes like doves, and his legs pillars of marble.
The daughters offer to seek him, and she says he has gone down to his vineyard to pasture his flock among the lilies.
